name: China Masters
stakes: This Super 750 event offers India's top shuttlers a crucial opportunity to consolidate rankings, build momentum, and make a statement on the global stage following the World Championships.
summary:
India arrives at the China Masters, a Super 750 event, with a strong contingent looking to make a significant impact. All eyes will be on the Men's Doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who are the sole seeded Indian entry at World No. 5. Coming off a quarterfinal finish at the World Championships, their fitness will be a key factor as they navigate a challenging field.

The Women's Doubles duo of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand Pullela ride a wave of confidence after their historic bronze medal at the recent World Championships—a performance that firmly places them among the world's elite. In singles, PV Sindhu (World No. 10) and Lakshya Sen (World No. 13) will be eager to rebound after earlier-than-expected exits at the Worlds, aiming to find their rhythm and make deep runs here. Veteran HS Prannoy, ranked 24, also seeks a strong showing.

India's top Mixed Doubles pair, Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto, continue their ascent, while young Malvika Bansod looks to gain valuable experience against top-tier competition. With no specific draws announced yet, the Indian camp will be keenly awaiting their opening matchups, hoping for favorable pathways to the later stages of this crucial tournament.
